articles.full_text:
अल नीनो का डबल अटैक: गर्मी, बारिश के बाद अब सर्दियों पर संकट; भारत समेत दुनियाभर में अलर्ट
अल नीनो के कारण भारत दोहरी मौसमी चुनौती का सामना कर रहा है, जिससे मानसून में कमी के बाद अब ...और पढ़ें
HighLights
अल नीनो 2027 तक दुनिया को प्रभावित कर सकता है।
भारत में मानसून के बाद सर्दियों में तापमान बढ़ने की आशंका।
कृषि और जल संसाधनों पर दबाव बढ़ने की चिंता।
डिजिटल डेस्क, नई दिल्ली। वैश्विक जलवायु से आ रहे तेजी से बदलावों के बीच अल नीनो ने पूरी दुनिया को अलर्ट पर रख दिया है। भारत के लिए यह मौसमी बदलाव दोहरी चुनौती बनकर सामने आ रहा है।
मानसून के दौरान 13 प्रतिशत कम बारिश होने के बाद, अब सबकी नजरें इस बात पर टिकी हैं कि क्या यह मौसमी घटना सर्दियों में तापमान बढ़ाएगी, क्या ये बारिश के पैटर्न को बिगाड़ेगी और क्या कृषि पर दबाव बढ़ाएगी?
इंडोनेशिया में धधकती भयानक जंगलों की आग से लेकर प्रशांत महासागर में तूफानों की असामान्य सक्रियता तक अल नीनो का असर दुनिया के लगभग हर कोने में देखने को मिल रहा है। अब सवाल यह है कि आने वाले महीनों में और मज़बूत होते अल नीनो का भारत पर क्या असर पड़ सकता है।
2027 तक बना रह सकता है असर
विश्व मौसम विज्ञान संगठन (WMO) की रिपोर्ट के अनुसार अल नीनो कई महीनों से लगातार मजबूत हो रहा है। WMO ने चेतावनी जारी की है कि यह घटना 2026 के अंत तक और अधिक तीव्र हो सकती है और इसका प्रभाव 2027 तक बना रह सकता है।
इस असामान्य मौसमी गतिविधि के कारण आने वाले समय में दुनिया भर में अलग-अलग क्षेत्रों में अत्यधिक तापमान, अनिश्चित बारिश और अन्य प्राकृतिक आपदाओं का खतरा काफी बढ़ गया है।
भारत के लिए सबसे बड़ी चिंता यह है कि क्या मजबूत होता अल नीनो, मानसून की कमी के असर को और बढ़ा देगा? साथ ही क्या यह आने वाले महीनों में सर्दियों के तापमान, बारिश और कृषि की स्थितियों को प्रभावित करेगा?
क्या है अल नीनो?
अल नीनो एक मौसमी घटना है, जिसमें मध्य और पूर्वी भूमध्यरेखीय प्रशांत महासागर में समुद्र की सतह का तापमान असामान्य रूप से गर्म हो जाता है। यह अल नीनो-सदर्न ऑसिलेशन (ENSO) का गर्म चरण है। यह एक प्राकृतिक मौसमी पैटर्न है जो दुनिया भर में वायुमंडलीय परिसंचरण, हवाओं के तंत्र और बारिश के वितरण को प्रभावित करता है।
अल नीनो भारत के मौसम को कैसे प्रभावित करता है?
भारत के मामले में अल नीनो पर कड़ी नजर रखी जाती है, क्योंकि आमतौर पर इसके कारण दक्षिण-पश्चिम मानसून के दौरान सामान्य से कम बारिश होने का खतरा बढ़ जाता है।
प्रशांत महासागर के पानी का तापमान बढ़ने से वैश्विक हवाओं और वायुमंडलीय परिसंचरण का पैटर्न बदल जाता है। यह बदलाव उन मौसमी स्थितियों को काफी कमजोर कर देता है जो भारतीय मानसून के लिए मददगार होती हैं। इससे लंबे समय तक सूखा रहने और बारिश की कमी होने की संभावना बढ़ जाती है।
भारत में असान बारिश और असाधारण सूखा
बीते मानसूनी सीजन में भारत के अलग-अलग हिस्सों में बारिश का असमान वितरण देखने को मिला। मध्य भारत में तो लगभग सामान्य बारिश हुई, लेकिन पूर्वी और पूर्वात्तर भारत में 26 प्रतिशत की कमी दर्ज की गई जिसे असाधारण सूखा माना जा सकता है।
वहीं दक्षिणी राज्यों में भी औसत से 24 प्रतिशत कम बारिश हुई। अल नीनो के और मजबूत होने से भारत के कुछ हिस्सों में सामान्य से ज्यादा गर्मी हो सकती है, जिससे जल संसाधनों और कृषि पर दबाव बढ़ सकता है।
सर्दियों में तापमान बढ़ने की संभावना
विश्व मौसम विज्ञान संगठन (WMO) ने 'साउथ एशियन क्लाइमेट आउटलुक फोरम' का हवाला देते हुए अनुमान लगाया है कि अक्टूबर-दिसंबर 2026 के दौरान दक्षिण एशिया के अधिकांश हिस्सों में अधिकतम और न्यूनतम तापमान सामान्य या उससे अधिक रह सकता है।
सर्दियों के आखिर में तापमान बढ़ने से गेहूं की पैदावार पर खतरा आ सकता है, खासकर अगर यह गर्मी गेहूं में दाने भरने के समय के दौरान पड़े। हालांकि इसका वास्तविक असर उस समय के मौसम पर निर्भर करेगा। वहीं जनवरी और फरवरी के हालात जलवायु के बदलते पैटर्न जैसे कि वेस्टर्न डिस्टर्बेंस पर निर्भर करेंगे।
अल नीनो का वैश्विक विनाशकारी रूप
अल नीनो केवल भारत तक सीमित नहीं है, बल्कि इसका वैश्विक असर बेहद खतरनाक मोड़ ले रहा है। भयंकर गर्मी और सूखे के कारण इंडोनेशिया वर्ष 2015 के बाद से सबसे भयानक जंगल की आग का सामना कर रहा है। पूर्वी अफ्रीका के कुछ क्षेत्रों में जहां भयानक सूखे की स्थिति है, वहीं कुछ अन्य हिस्सों में बेमौसम भारी बारिश और भीषण बाढ़ का प्रकोप दिख रहा है।
पूर्वी प्रशांत क्षेत्र में उष्णकटिबंधीय तूफानों की गतिविधि असामान्य रूप से तेज हो गई है, जबकि अटलांटिक क्षेत्र में ऊपरी हवाओं के प्रभाव से तूफान बनने की प्रक्रिया बाधित हुई है। अमेजन के जंगलों में सूखे के हालात बने हुए हैं, जबकि दक्षिण अमेरिका के निचले इलाकों में बाढ़ का खतरा मंडरा रहा है।
क्या है भारत के सामने रास्ते?
आने वाले महीनों में अल नीनो का बढ़ता असर भारत के जल संसाधनों, कृषि पैदावार और खाद्य सुरक्षा के लिए एक बड़ी परीक्षा साबित होने वाला है। सरकार और कृषि विभागों को किसानों के लिए समय पर एडवाइजरी जारी करने, कम पानी वाली फसलों को बढ़ावा देने और जलाशयों में पानी के सही प्रबंधन पर ध्यान केंद्रित करना होगा ताकि संभावित खाद्य संकट से बचा जा सके।

World News in Brief: Aid for Ethiopia, Abyei drone strikes condemned, extreme heat and newborn health
The World Health Organization (WHO) is scaling up emergency health response operations across Afar, Amhara and Tigray in Ethiopia to address growing humanitarian and health needs resulting from ongoing hostilities.
The UN health agency has strengthened its emergency coordination, deployed technical teams and expanded operational support to keep essential health services running in conflict-affected areas of the north.
Working with regional authorities, WHO is supporting preparedness, response coordination, disease surveillance and lifesaving interventions in collaboration with a range of partners, including the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) and the UN refugee agency, UNHCR.
71 tonnes of supplies
WHO has delivered more than 71 metric tonnes of essential supplies to Tigray, Amhara and Afar.
Aid includes emergency health kits, cholera response materials, reproductive health kits and medicine for noncommunicable diseases.
The agency is also backing outbreak investigation, vaccine distribution and emergency referrals while strengthening public health monitoring in areas affected by insecurity and displacement.
Mobile teams and facilities continue to provide essential services, including primary care, disease prevention and maternal and reproductive health services.
Guterres deplores recent deadly attack in Abyei
UN Secretary-General António Guterres has urged authorities in Sudan and South Sudan to act to avert further attacks in the disputed Abyei border region.
The Secretary-General strongly condemned deadly drone strikes near a busy market on Monday that killed dozens of civilians, injured many others and set structures ablaze.
“I express my deepest and heartfelt condolences to the families of those who lost their lives and wish a swift recovery to the injured,” he said in a statement published late on Wednesday.
He noted that in the aftermath of the attack, the UN peacekeeping force in Abyei (UNISFA) deployed medical personnel, firefighting equipment and quick reaction forces to provide emergency treatment, support casualty evacuation and prevent the fire from spreading.
Respect and protect civilians
The strikes on Amiet Market and the Todach area are among the latest developments in the war between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and former allies the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) that erupted in April 2023.
The Secretary-General stressed that attacks targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure are prohibited under international law.
“I remind that all parties to the armed conflict must comply with their obligations under international humanitarian law, including to respect and protect civilians at all times,” he said, underlining the need for accountability and calling on the Governments of South Sudan and Sudan “to take all steps possible to help prevent further attacks and uphold Abyei’s demilitarised status”.
New tool tracks heat’s impact on pregnancy, newborns and children
Extreme heat can put lives at risk even before birth. It also raises health risks during pregnancy and for newborns and young children.
To help countries track these dangers, a group of UN agencies has launched the first set of priority indicators focused on these vulnerable groups.
“Our health systems need the data to recognise this reality and take action,” said Bruce Gordon, interim director of environment, climate change, One Health and migration at the World Health Organization (WHO).
That means everything from protecting people during heatwaves to building climate risk into everyday health services, he added.
WHO, the World Meteorological Organization (WMO), UNICEF and the UN reproductive health agency, UNFPA, launched the new framework designed to strengthen preparedness, improve monitoring and accelerate response.
Improved heat-health planning
The new report recommends that countries monitor pre-term births, stillbirths, low birthweight, pregnancy hypertension, child deaths and health-facility visits during extreme heat.
Monitoring school attendance can also help reveal how heat is disrupting children’s lives.
An estimated 1.5 billion children worldwide are exposed to heatwaves that are becoming more frequent, longer or more severe.
The new information can help health governments prepare facilities for rising demand, strengthen warnings to pregnant women and families, identify communities at greatest risk and improve planning, the agencies said.

articles.full_text:
Namibians have been warned to prepare for temperatures of up to 42°C as a heatwave continues across the country until the weekend.
The Namibia Meteorological Service says temperatures are expected to range between 36°C and 42°C for the rest of the week and into the weekend.
On Wednesday, the weather service said the heatwave is caused by a strong high-pressure system moving slowly from northern Namibia towards the central parts of the country.
The system causes air to sink and warm, resulting in high temperatures.
The weather service said the regions expected to be hardest hit are Zambezi, Kavango East, Kavango West, Ohangwena, Oshikoto, Oshana, Omusati, Kunene and Otjozondjupa.
The heatwave is expected to reach the Khomas region by Friday before spreading to southern Namibia over the weekend.
The weather service has warned that prolonged exposure to high temperatures could cause dehydration, heat exhaustion and heatstroke.
It has urged members of the public to drink plenty of water and avoid spending long periods outdoors, particularly between 12h00 and 15h00, when temperatures are at their highest.
People are also advised to stay in shaded or well-ventilated areas to reduce their exposure to the heat.
The weather service urged families and communities to pay particular attention to elderly people and babies, who may be more vulnerable to extreme temperatures.

articles.full_text:
Classrooms could soon look different as Malawi braces for scorching temperatures of up to 42°C, forcing schools to take urgent measures to protect learners from the dangerous heat.
The Ministry of Education, Science and Technology has directed schools and learning institutions across Malawi to take immediate measures to protect learners from the heatwave
In a press release the ministry said the measures follow a heatwave warning issued by the Department of Climate Change and Meteorological Services (DCCMS) for October 18–23, 2026.
The ministry said unusually high temperatures are also affecting parts of the Northern and Central regions, as well as lakeshore areas, raising concerns about the safety of learners and teachers.
Schools, including Early Childhood Development Centres, have been urged to introduce flexible learning arrangements, adjust timetables and relax uniform requirements where necessary to reduce learners’ exposure to excessive heat.
The ministry has also directed schools to suspend or reschedule sports, assemblies, parades and manual work between 10am and 3pm, when temperatures are likely to pose greater risks.
Institutions have further been advised to ensure continuous access to safe drinking water, encourage regular hydration and keep classrooms cool and well ventilated. Schools should also use shaded areas and reduce overcrowding.
The ministry said the precautions are intended to safeguard learners, teachers and support staff while ensuring that learning continues during the period of unusually high temperatures.

Thiruvananthapuram, Kollam, Pathanamthitta, Alappuzha and Kottayam are under orange alert, with isolated very heavy rainfall likely over the next 24 hours, the India Meteorological Department said in its latest update
Thiruvananthapuram: Several parts of Keralam received rain accompanied by thunder and lightning on Wednesday, with the IMD issuing an orange alert in five districts and a yellow alert in five others.
Thiruvananthapuram, Kollam, Pathanamthitta, Alappuzha and Kottayam are under orange alert, with isolated very heavy rainfall likely over the next 24 hours, the India Meteorological Department said in its latest update.
Idukki, Ernakulam, Thrissur, Palakkad and Malappuram are under yellow alert for isolated heavy rainfall of 64.5 mm to 115.5 mm, it said.
The Keralam State Disaster Management Authority (KSDMA) said precautionary sirens would sound on Wednesday evening in the five orange-alert districts.
The IMD has advised against fishing along the Keralam and Lakshadweep coasts from Oct 21 to 25 in view of the prevailing weather conditions.
In view of the alerts, the KSDMA urged people living in landslide-, mudslide- and flash flood-prone areas to move to safer locations as directed by authorities. Those living along riverbanks and downstream of dams were advised to relocate if instructed to do so.
Residents of disaster-prone areas were asked to check the availability of relief camps and move to them during daylight hours, in coordination with local self-government and revenue authorities.
The KSDMA advised people not to cross rivers or enter water bodies for bathing, fishing or other activities during heavy rain. It cautioned against gathering on bridges over water bodies to take photographs or selfies.
People were advised to avoid unnecessary travel during intense rainfall and to postpone trips to waterfalls, other water bodies and hilly areas until the warnings were withdrawn.
Motorists were urged to exercise caution on roads near water bodies and on stretches under repair. They were told not to drive through flooded areas or cross overflowing waterways.
Taluk and district-level control rooms are functioning round the clock across the state, the KSDMA said. People can call the toll-free numbers 1077 and 1070 for assistance or to report potential dangers.
An orange alert signifies very heavy rainfall of 115.6 mm to 204.4 mm, and a yellow alert signifies heavy rainfall of 64.5 mm to 115.5 mm.

The India Meteorological Department has placed five Kerala districts under an orange alert, warning of isolated very heavy rainfall over the next 24 hours as intense rain, thunder and lightning affect several parts of the state. Thiruvananthapuram, Kollam, Pathanamthitta, Alappuzha and Kottayam are covered by the warning.
The IMD has also issued a yellow alert for Idukki, Ernakulam, Thrissur, Palakkad and Malappuram, where isolated heavy rainfall measuring between 64.5 mm and 115.5 mm is likely. An orange alert indicates very heavy rainfall between 115.6 mm and 204.4 mm, while a yellow alert denotes heavy rainfall between 64.5 mm and 115.5 mm.
The Kerala State Disaster Management Authority said precautionary sirens would sound on Wednesday evening in the five orange-alert districts. It urged residents in landslide-, mudslide- and flash-flood-prone areas to move to safer locations when directed by authorities.
People living along riverbanks and downstream of dams were advised to relocate if instructed to do so. The disaster management authority also asked residents in vulnerable areas to check the availability of relief camps and move to them during daylight hours in coordination with local self-government and revenue authorities.
The advisories carry direct implications for movement across roads, bridges and low-lying areas. The KSDMA asked residents to avoid unnecessary travel during intense rainfall and to postpone trips to waterfalls, other water bodies and hilly areas until the warnings are withdrawn. Motorists were told not to drive through flooded stretches or attempt to cross overflowing waterways, and to exercise caution on roads near water bodies and on sections undergoing repair.
The authority warned people not to cross rivers or enter water bodies for bathing, fishing or other activities during heavy rain. It also cautioned against gathering on bridges to take photographs or selfies, a recurring safety concern during periods of swollen rivers and fast-moving water.
The IMD has advised against fishing along the Kerala and Lakshadweep coasts from October 21 to 25 because of the prevailing weather conditions. The restriction affects fishing activity along the coast and forms part of the wider precautionary response to the weather system.
Taluk- and district-level control rooms are functioning around the clock across Kerala, the KSDMA said. Residents seeking assistance or reporting potential dangers can contact the toll-free numbers 1077 and 1070.
The immediate response places responsibility on district and local authorities to communicate evacuation instructions, maintain access to relief facilities and respond to hazards in vulnerable settlements. Residents in the alert areas have been advised to follow official directions and avoid exposed locations until the warnings are withdrawn.

Wednesday, 21 October 2026, 18:45
PHOTO BGNES
Font size
Brief showers and thunderstorms are expected in places across western Bulgaria on Thursday night. The lowest temperatures will range from 8°C to 13°C, around 10°C in Sofia.
The morning will be cloudy across the country. Cloud cover will briefly break up during the day before increasing again from the west, bringing rain to parts of western Bulgaria. From the afternoon and throughout the night into Friday, an approaching cold front will bring heavy and locally significant rainfall to many parts of the country, accompanied by thunderstorms.
Winds will be moderate, becoming strong in eastern Bulgaria and north of the mountains, from the south-southwest. Maximum temperatures will range from 20°C to 25°C, around 19°C in the capital city.
Along the Black Sea coast, scattered rain is possible in the north. In the afternoon, skies in the south will clear, giving way to sunny weather. Daytime highs will range from 18°C to 23°C. The seawater temperature is 17°C-18°C. Sea state 2 on the Beaufort scale.
In the mountains, the weather will be mostly cloudy. Rain, temporarily heavy at times and accompanied by thunderstorms, will begin in the west before noon. At the highest peaks of the Rila and Pirin mountains, rain will mix with snow. Maximum temperatures will reach around 15°C at an altitude of 1,200 metres and 9°C at 2,000 metres.
On Friday, a cold front will move across the country, bringing mostly cloudy skies and rain to many areas. Heavy rainfall is expected in some parts of central and eastern Bulgaria. Winds will shift to the northwest and strengthen, bringing colder air. Daytime temperatures will drop by 5–6 degrees.
Edited by Ivo Ivanov
Translated by Kostadin Atanasov
